body:
I said I was done escalating and I am, but I owe you one confirmed fact on the single open ask I left you, because I had it from a reviewer report rather than from the package.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY:

  formals(plan_crossnobis)$metric
  #> shrinkage_precision()

So the default is real. plan_crossnobis() selects a shrinkage covariance estimator on the user behalf, with a shrinkage intensity chosen by the function rather than by the analyst.

Set against R/pairing.R:50-53 and R/pairing.R:108, where the package refuses to let independence be assumed and forces the user to state it because it is a claim about their data, the two positions look inconsistent to me. A shrinkage intensity is at least as much a statistical choice as a pairing independence assertion, and it is arguably more consequential for the resulting distances, since it enters the metric that defines them.

I am not filing this as a usability bead and I am not proposing a change. It is a semantics question about a default that predates this review, it sits in the chain you certified, and you will know whether it was deliberated or inherited. If it was deliberated, the reasoning is worth a line in the docs, because from outside it reads as an inconsistency.

Two other things verified since I last wrote, both of which confirm reviewer reports I had been repeating without checking:

  rdm(crossnobis_plan) and rsa(crossnobis_plan) both fail with "requires a geometry plan or
  complete effect form". The gate is R/views.R:104-108. So the crossnobis-to-RDM branch really
  is missing, and the error a user gets is a contradiction on its face - they hold an object of
  class effect_crossnobis_plan, built by a function named plan_crossnobis, and are told the verb
  requires a plan. Filed.

  R/views.R:269-273 does branch on plan versus form and route to evaluate_geometry for plans,
  which is the mechanism my withdrawn wrapper warning turned on. Confirmed rather than assumed
  this time.

Nothing here needs an answer. The shrinkage default is the only item I would still value your view on whenever you resume.
